title: Dean Blevins: Sooner Quarterback Turned Oklahoma Sportscaster
question: Which former OU quarterback became a longtime Oklahoma City sports anchor?
answer: Dean Blevins, a Sooner quarterback in the mid-1970s under Barry Switzer, became a longtime Oklahoma City sportscaster and led News 9's sports desk until retiring in 2025.
summary: Dean Blevins quarterbacked Oklahoma in the mid-1970s, then built a four-decade Oklahoma City sportscasting career with Emmys and a Journalism Hall of Fame nod.
body: Plenty of former Sooners end up on television, but few have been as woven into Oklahoma sports coverage as Dean Blevins. A Norman High School standout, he was an all-state athlete in football, basketball and track in 1974 and was named the state's top high school athlete before heading to the University of Oklahoma.

At OU he played quarterback for Barry Switzer's Sooners in the mid-1970s, a stretch that included two national championship teams, in 1974 and 1975. Reference sources list his years as the Sooners' quarterback as 1974 and 1975.

Broadcasting became his second career. He worked as a sports director at KOCO-TV in Oklahoma City in the late 1980s and early 1990s, then moved to KWTV, the station now branded News 9. He became its lead sports anchor and sports director in 2001 and hosted weekly programs with Oklahoma football coach Bob Stoops for years.

The honors piled up. News 9 reports that he won two Emmy Awards and was named Oklahoma Sportscaster of the Year eight times. In February 2025 the station announced that he would retire as sports director effective July 1 after 41 years in sports media, and that he was to be inducted into the Oklahoma Journalism Hall of Fame that May.
For a generation of fans, the voice breaking down a Sooners game on the evening news once took the snaps himself.
